content.title: About
content.content: Almond butter is a paste made by grinding whole almonds into a smooth, creamy consistency. It has a mild nutty flavor, a slightly sweet aroma, and a velvety texture that works well for spreading, sauces, and baking.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Almond butter retains almost all the nutrients of whole almonds in a more convenient form.
The first commercial production of almond butter began in the United States in the early 1920s.
Unlike peanut butter, almond butter does not contain aflatoxins because almonds are less prone to mold.
It is a popular vegan alternative to dairy butter in many recipes.
Creamy almond butter can stay fresh longer than whole nuts due to reduced exposure to oxygen.

items.title: Rich in vitamin E
items.content: Vitamin E is a powerful antioxidant that protects cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Provides healthy monounsaturated fats
items.content: Monounsaturated fats support heart health and help lower LDL cholesterol.

items.title: Contains magnesium
items.content: Magnesium is essential for muscle function, nerve signaling, and blood sugar regulation.

items.title: Provides plant protein and fiber
items.content: Protein aids tissue repair, while fiber promotes digestive health and satiety.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: Calcium is important for bones and teeth, and almond butter offers it in an easy-to-use form.

items.title: Tree nut allergy
items.content: People allergic to almonds or other tree nuts may experience severe reactions.

items.title: High in calories
items.content: One tablespoon contains about 100 kcal, so portion control is advisable.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: Almonds contain oxalates, which can contribute to kidney stone formation in susceptible individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Use almond butter as a spread on toast, stir it into smoothies, incorporate it into sauces, dressings, baked goods, and desserts. It is also frequently used in vegan recipes as a butter substitute.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store almond butter in an airtight jar in a cool, dark place. For longer shelf life, keep it refrigerated to prevent fat oxidation. Discard if it develops a rancid smell or off‑color.
